resources.string: No sound is reaching the microphone
Birding needs the BirdNET model, about 39MB. It is downloaded once and then works with no network.\n\nThe model is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and may not be used commercially.
Keep the sound of each detection, so tapping its row plays back what was heard. About 288KB each, in the app\'s own storage rather than in your music.
Reset settings — tap again to confirm
Not listening. Nothing is being recorded.
List a bird heard over and over as one line for the run, or as every hearing with its own time.
Which microphone input to record from. Unprocessed is the rawest, and the one the recogniser expects.
How sure the recogniser has to be before a bird is written down. Lower catches more, and is wrong more often.
Throw away everything below this pitch before listening, against traffic or wind. 0 leaves the sound alone.
Take the audio from a connected Bluetooth microphone rather than from the phone itself.
Give a fixed latitude and longitude instead of using GPS. With this on the app never asks for location permission at all.
Put the picture of the last bird heard clearly at the top of the listening screen. It stays there until a different bird is heard as clearly.
Throw away the model\'s non-bird answers: people, dogs, engines, sirens, tools and plain noise.
Restore — this replaces the log; tap again
That file is not a backup this app wrote
Delete the log — tap again to confirm
Draw the shape of the recording under the photograph when a row is opened: time across, pitch up, loud dark.
Keep recordings for this session only

Identification happens on this phone. The only thing fetched is a bird's photograph, and only for a row you open.

A fork of whoBIRD by woheller69. GNU General Public Licence v3.
